# AgentCore harness-tools — AUDITED 2026-09-26 (FIRST AUDIT). [REPORTED]
# Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-tools.html

FIVE tool types + 2 builtins.
  1. remote_mcp                  config.remoteMcp.url  (+ optional .headers map)
  2. agentcore_gateway           config.agentCoreGateway.gatewayArn (+ .outboundAuth)
  3. agentcore_browser           no config
  4. agentcore_code_interpreter  no config
  5. inline_function             config.inlineFunction.description + .inputSchema
  BUILTINS always present unless restricted: `shell` (bash), `file_operations`
  (view/create/edit). ~900 input tokens of definitions added to EVERY model request.

tools settable at CreateHarness, UpdateHarness AND InvokeHarness (per-invocation override).
CLI: `agentcore add tool --harness X --type <underscore_name>`; persisted in harness.json.

*** remote_mcp headers can hold RAW PLAINTEXT SECRETS. ***
  Doc's own example: {"Authorization": "Bearer <your-token>"}.
  Alternative: ${arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:<region>:<acct>:token-vault/default/
  apikeycredentialprovider/<name>} resolved at invocation time.
  AWS recommends Gateway + AgentCore Identity "for managed credential rotation and
  OAuth-protected tools" — i.e. the plaintext path is documented and supported.
  ANY public MCP endpoint by URL, "No Gateway required for simple cases" =>
  no policy enforcement, no inbound/outbound auth, no access control on that path.

allowedTools — LLM-selection scoping only. Patterns:
  "*" | "shell" | "file_*" | "@builtin" | "@builtin/shell" | "@git" | "@git/git_status"
  | "@git/read_*" | "@*-mcp/status".  Omitted => ALL tools allowed (fail-open default).
*** VERBATIM: "allowedTools scopes LLM tool selection during InvokeHarness only. It does
    not affect InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand, which is a separate API with its own IAM action
    (bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand) that executes commands directly without
    passing through the LLM. To prevent direct command execution, do not grant
    bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand in your IAM policies." ***

inline_function = executes CLIENT-SIDE, not on the harness VM. Harness pauses with
  stopReason "tool_use", returns toolUse to caller code, caller posts back a toolResult
  on the SAME runtimeSessionId. Harness stores the AUTHORITATIVE assistant toolUse in
  session state and IGNORES a resent copy. Missing/duplicate/stale/replayed result cannot
  resume the handoff. Documented pattern for "human-in-the-loop approvals".
*** Doc warns: read harness-lifecycle-hooks.md#harness-hook-inline-functions BEFORE using
    an `after_tool_call` event for an inline function "as an authorization or audit
    signal." => the obvious audit hook is NOT reliable for this tool type. ***

WEB SEARCH is not a harness tool type. It arrives as an agentcore_gateway whose target has
  connectorId: "web-search", exposed as MCP tool `WebSearch`. Gateway service role needs
  bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch; harness execution role needs
  bedrock-agentcore:InvokeGateway on the gateway ARN. us-east-1 only. Served entirely
  within AWS on a purpose-built index.

Gateway outbound auth choices in the TUI: AWS IAM (default) | None | OAuth.
  "None" is a selectable outbound-auth mode.
